chapters.title: Three hidden taxes and the four billing layers
The context tax and the reasoning tax
The autonomous tax and the November 2026 credit cliff
Auditing spend: Cost Management, consumption estimator and token flow maps
Four levers: semantic caching, LLMLingua compression, model routing, PTU vs PAYG
Guardrails, the 90-day roadmap and the governance model
Case study: rebuilding the Contoso support agent
Advanced scenarios, emergency brakes and the weekly checklist

takeaways: Most AI agent cost comes from architecture, not model pricing: bloated retrieval context, sending every request to the flagship model, and autonomous agents consuming Copilot credits unchecked.

Four levers compound when applied together: semantic caching in Azure API Management, prompt compression with LLMLingua, model routing in Azure AI Foundry, and buying capacity correctly with PAYG or yearly PTU only at sustained high utilization.

Cost control lasts only with governance: tag every resource, classify agents into gold, silver and bronze cost classes before they are built, and enforce budgets, credit caps and rate limits automatically.
hook: Your Azure OpenAI and Copilot Studio bills keep climbing even when usage looks flat. This episode is for architects, platform teams and FinOps leads running AI agents in the Microsoft cloud, and it shows how to find the context, reasoning and autonomous taxes and remove them with caching, compression, routing and governance.
